ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Corporate UBO: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9, as amended by the Business Corporations Amendment Act, 2023, creating the Alberta Beneficial Ownership Registry; administered by Service Alberta and the Alberta Corporate Registry under the Corporations Information Act, RSA 2000, c. C-28 and the Alberta Corporations Regulation, AR 199/2000. AML/CFT: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and regulations (PCMLTFR); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c. C-46, Part XII.2; FINTRAC supervision; Canadian sanctions administered by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c. 17, the United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c. U-2, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2017, c. 21. Federal equivalent: sections 21.1-21.5 of the Canada Business Corporations Act (public beneficial ownership register operational January 22, 2024). ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 no-code software building is not a licensed activity in Alberta; no MSB classification is triggered because all SaaS payment facilitation is performed by regulated third parties (Stripe as PSP, Paddle as merchant of record).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Fully_Public (Alberta Beneficial Ownership Registry publicly searchable under the 2023 statutory regime; the federal CBCA register is also fully public since January 22, 2024)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: NUANS corporate name search report (mandatory pre-filing evidence of name distinctiveness)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Alberta Corporate Registry via licensed NUANS service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic administrative document, self-authenticating within Canada; if presented to a foreign bank or registry, apostille by the Justice and Solicitor General of Alberta (Canada party to the Hague Apostille Convention effective January 11, 2024)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport and proof of residential address for each director, officer, and individual with significant control (UBO at the 25% plus one share threshold)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner for oaths in the document holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the source country (for US, UK, EU and other Apostille states) OR consular legalization at the competent Canadian embassy or consulate in the source country (for non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory declaration, director consent form, and register of individuals with significant control (UBO register) executed by each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Alberta commissioner for oaths or notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization only within Canada; if relied upon in a non-Hague jurisdiction, chain authentication through Global Affairs Canada plus consular legalization at the destination country's mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of corporate existence or good standing of any foreign corporate shareholder or upstream parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry (e.g., a US Secretary of State or Companies House)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the foreign registry's competent authority, recognized in Canada without further legalization since January 11, 2024; alternatively, consular legalization at the Canadian mission in the source country for non-Hague jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, negative-media, and sanctions screening of all directors, officers, UBOs (25% or greater), and authorized signatories at onboarding and annually thereafter: (1) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (2) Global Affairs Canada consolidated Canadian autonomous sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act, and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (3) OFAC SDN List, mandatory because USD payment rails through Stripe are US-intermediated; (4) FINTRAC and RCMP watchlists; (5) EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists as secondary coverage; (6) PEP database per FATF Recommendation 12 and FINTRAC guidance. Foreign PEPs require enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds, and source-of-wealth verification. Stripe and Paddle will independently re-verify the entity and its UBOs under their own KYC and payment-facilitator onboarding. All Pre-Incorporation KYC results must be archived for a minimum of five years in accordance with PCMLTFA record-keeping requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - online portal at corporate-registry.alberta.ca; filings accepted electronically through the government portal and licensed authorized service providers; NUANS pre-screening against federal, provincial, and extra-provincial databases
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Per section 10 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) and applicable name regulations, the corporate name must be in English or French or a hyphenated bilingual form; may contain Latin-script letters, numerals, and permitted punctuation; foreign-language or non-Latin source words must be transliterated into Latin script, and if distinctiveness is claimed through the foreign element a certified translation is required; every name must contain a mandatory legal element (Inc., Corp., Ltd., Incorporated, Corporation, or French equivalents Ltée and Incorporee); the name must be distinctive and must not be confusingly similar to any existing name, registered trademark, or extra-provincial registered name found in the NUANS database
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banker, Trust, Trustco, Insurance, Assurance, Loan, Finance (require prior financial-services licensing and ministerial consent)
Royal, Crown, Police, Province of Alberta, Government, or any token implying Crown or governmental connection (written consent or ministerial approval required)
University, College, Institute, Academy, Chamber of Commerce (require authorization or written permission of the responsible body)
Co-operative, Co-op (require incorporation under the Cooperatives Act, not the Business Corporations Act)
Canada, Canadian (generally restricted to federal-namespace corporations; unavailable to ordinary Alberta provincial corporations without ministerial approval)
Obscene, scandalous, misleading, or misdescriptive terms, third-party trademarks, and names implying association with a real enterprise or person without consent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation under section 17 of the ABCA is valid for 90 days from the date of the NUANS report and may be renewed once for an additional 90 days by payment of the registry reservation fee; any renewal beyond the initial window requires a fresh NUANS report at CAD 75 to CAD 90. Rejection appeal procedure: (1) within 30 days of the refusal notice, file a written Request for Reconsideration with the Director, Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), attaching the original NUANS report, a distinguishability and confusion analysis, any consent or watch letters from prior name owners, and relevant trademark evidence; (2) the Director issues a written decision within 30-45 days; (3) if the decision remains unfavorable, the applicant must select an alternative name and order a new NUANS report because no name hold attaches during the appeal; (4) final recourse is judicial review before the Alberta Court of King's Bench, limited to errors of law or jurisdiction. Practical protocol: file two or three alternative names in a single incorporation package to avoid operational delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with strict conformity: the ABCA requires a registered office with a physical street address in Alberta open for service of process and official mail during ordinary business hours; a PO Box address alone is prohibited. For a digital low-code and website template builder under ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210, a licensed registered-agent or virtual-office service providing a physical Alberta street address, dedicated mailbox, certified mail handling, and business-hours document access is fully compliant without any requirement for local employees, server presence, or physical operational premises. The corporation must, however, maintain its statutory records (minute book, register of directors, register of individuals with significant control, and share register) at the Alberta registered office or at another location in Canada designated by the directors and properly notified to the registry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated 3-5% probability within the first 12 months for a fully digital, non-licensed, low-risk ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 SaaS entity. Unannounced physical premises inspections are not a routine ABCA enforcement mechanism; compliance is verified through annual returns, UBO register filings, and correspondence directed to the registered office. The registered-office provider should be instructed to scan and forward all official mail to the founders' permanent address on the same business day to ensure no statutory notice is missed.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via licensed NUANS service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff approximately CAD 75 (CAD 2 per search line plus research report fee); prevailing market rate CAD 75-90

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per the corporate registry fee schedule: CAD 100 for online filing, CAD 175 for paper filing; no separate certificate processing fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and corporate records address service (first year; licensed registered agent with physical Alberta street address and same-day mail forwarding)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registry compliance: preparation, execution, and initial filing of the register of individuals with significant control (25% threshold) and annual ownership confirmation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9 (ABCA), ss. 6-9 (incorporation and certificate), s. 17 (registered office), Part 8 (directors) and Part 11 (corporate records); Alberta Business Corporations Regulations and related forms.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry of Corporations, Service Alberta (Alberta Corporate Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation filed under the Alberta Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. An Alberta business corporation may authorize and issue shares with no par value. The first directors must fix lawful consideration for share subscriptions. No escrow account or capital escrow is required for an ordinary private software/no-code development corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Articles of Incorporation filed under the Alberta Business Corporations Act are adopted, and the Company is confirmed as duly organized. (2) The registered office is fixed at [address], Alberta, with [name] as registered office contact. (3) The initial subscribers are allotted [number] common shares for lawful consideration, as approved by this board. (4) [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer. (5) The proposed by-laws, corporate seal, and banking resolutions are approved and entered in the minute book. (6) The officers are authorized to execute all filings and open bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized Registry Agent or the NUANS online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS search for the proposed corporate name and a backup name. Ensure the name is not confusingly similar to an existing Alberta or federal mark and includes a permitted corporate suffix such as Ltd., Corp., Inc. or ULC. If any consent or regulator approval is needed due to a sensitive name element, obtain that consent before filing. Attach the NUANS report and consents to the incorporation package.
required_dossiers: NUANS Name Search Report dated within 90 days
Proposed corporate name and backup name
Consents for non-conventional name elements, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a revised NUANS report with a new name and refile, or respond with a written objection argument and any required consents through the authorized Registry Agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator, proposed directors, and authorized Alberta Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Form 1, including share structure, restrictions on share transfers, first registered office, first directors, and any special provisions. All incorporating subscribers and first directors must execute the articles and director consent forms. Confirm that the registered office is an actual street address within Alberta and that the records address is also valid.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director forms for each proposed director
Registered Office Address and Records Address consent
List of initial directors and subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries execution, signature, consent, or content defects, correct the deficient form by obtaining proper signatures and submit a revised package. A replacement consent or corrected registered office address can be filed through the Registry Agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing, Payment, and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of Corporations, Service Alberta (Alberta Corporate Registry) via online filing system or authorized Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the completed Form 1 package to the Alberta Corporate Registry and pay the government filing fee. Retain the electronic filing acknowledgment. Once the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, verify the corporate name, filing number, date of incorporation, registered office, and directors exactly as intended before relying on the entity for contracts or tax registration.
required_dossiers: NUANS report and any name consent letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects or queries the application, cure identified deficiencies and resubmit without losing filed priority, subject to the Registry's resubmission rules. If the rejection is disputed on legal grounds, request formal review under the ABCA through the Registry's administrative review process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Corporate Records and Registered Office Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First directors of the Corporation (internal governance step)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first directors' meeting or adopt a written first board resolution. Adopt by-laws, fix the registered office and records address, appoint officers, approve a banking resolution, issue shares to subscribers, and open the corporate minute book and securities register. Ensure all resolutions are signed by the directors and filed in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Share subscription ledger and share certificates
Registered office consent from landlord or premises owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer declines appointment, elect a replacement by subsequent board resolution. If registered office consent is unavailable, obtain a valid consent from the premises owner and update the records address promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Program Account Enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register for the federal Business Number. Enrol for the corporate income tax account and, if required, GST/HST, payroll, and any provincial accounts. For an Alberta no-code software builder, GST/HST registration is mandatory once the small supplier threshold is exceeded or where taxable digital services are supplied in Canada. Provide supporting corporate documents as requested by CRA.
required_dossiers: First board resolution evidencing officer appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the registration or requests further proof, respond through My Business Account with corrected RC/BC forms and supporting corporate records. If a duplicate Business Number is identified, request consolidation or cancellation through CRA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registered Office Governance and Annual Return Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the registered office and records address in Alberta. File the first annual return with the Alberta Corporate Registry when due and keep director, officer, and registered address changes current. Maintain the required corporate records and make them available for review as required by the ABCA. Prepare final governance documents reflecting the number of directors, share transfers, and registered records address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return or an address change is queried, file a corrective filing through Registry Connect or the authorized Registry Agent and pay any applicable late filing fee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no Alberta industrial licensing board for a software publishing and no-code website builder activity under NAICS 511210; municipal land-use and business licensing authorities may apply if physical premises are used.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial statutory operating licence. A municipal business licence or home-occupation permit may be required by local by-law for the specific physical address.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA registration or full environmental assessment is triggered by an office-based no-code/software development operation; the activity is not a designated activity under Alberta's environmental assessment regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office-only operations produce no industrial process wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams. Sanitary wastewater discharge must comply with municipal sewer and plumbing codes. General occupational exposure limits under Alberta OHS law apply to office air quality and thermal conditions. Electronic waste from IT equipment must be handled in accordance with municipal waste bylaws and Alberta's electronic waste recycling obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Compliance with the Alberta Fire Code and municipal fire inspection requirements is required before occupancy. Building occupancy and structural load approvals must be obtained from the municipal building department. Alberta OHS Act requirements apply to the office workplace, including emergency planning, first aid, and hazard identification. No special civil defense clearance is required for a software/no-code service business.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); primary portal: My Business Account at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html and Business Registration Online (BRO). Alberta corporate income tax is collected by the CRA on behalf of Alberta Treasury Board and Finance under the federal-provincial Tax Collection Agreement; the Alberta Corporate Registry handles extra-provincial registration and provincial statute filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Canadian business corporation receives its 9-digit Business Number (BN) automatically upon incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Alberta Business Corporations Act. For foreign entities: (1) determine whether the non-resident corporation carries on business in Canada or makes taxable supplies in Canada; (2) register online through Business Registration Online (BRO) or by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) and Form RC1A (GST/HST account application); (3) appoint an authorized Canadian representative/agent if the non-resident has no physical Canadian presence; (4) obtain the mandatory BN program accounts, including the RT account for GST/HST and the RC account for Part I corporate tax; (5) the BN is the functional TIN/VAT ID for all CRA programs and must appear on invoices, GST/HST returns, and T2 corporate returns; no separate national TIN exists in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A Canadian Business Corporation is a separate person under Part I of the Income Tax Act and pays federal and Alberta corporate income tax in a single integrated T2 return; Canada has no pass-through or S-corp analogue and no federal check-the-box regime. The corporation is a separate GST/HST registrant. Non-resident hybrid entities such as US LLCs are recharacterized under the LLC conduit rules (ss. 94.1-94.3 of the Income Tax Act) and the Canada-US Treaty fiscal transparency protocol. Territorial scope: Canadian-resident corporations are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident corporations are taxed on Canadian-source business income under Part I and passive income under Part XIII withholding. Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box election. Elective and structured mechanisms include: (1) section 216 Income Tax Act election for a non-resident to report net Canadian rental income instead of gross Part XIII withholding; (2) section 217 Income Tax Act election for a non-resident employee to file net-income returns for Canadian employment income; (3) section 273 Excise Tax Act election for closely related GST/HST registrants to treat qualifying intra-group supplies as zero-rated; (4) Quick Method of Accounting election under section 229 ETA for small registrants; (5) mandatory hybrid-mismatch countermeasures under sections 18.2 and 18.3 of the Income Tax Act (no opt-out, aligned with BEPS Action 2); and (6) treaty-based relief mechanisms, including Form NR7 waiver applications, competent-authority mutual agreement procedures, and LLC fiscal-transparency characterization under the Canada-US Tax Convention. The Alberta Small Business Deduction (2% provincial rate on up to CAD 500,000 of active business income) is automatic and requires no affirmative election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST - Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax, imposed under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15). Alberta has no provincial sales tax and no HST; only the federal 5% GST applies to taxable supplies made in Alberta.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: a person making taxable supplies in Canada (including zero-rated supplies) must register for GST/HST once total worldwide taxable revenues, other than financial services, exceed CAD 30,000 per calendar year. Registration is voluntary below the threshold and is required for non-resident suppliers of specified digital services to Canadian consumers under the 2021 simplified non-resident registration regime once their Canadian taxable supplies exceed the same threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, API stamping, or digital fiscal invoicing. The CRA accepts paper or electronic invoices; a registered supplier's invoice must show the supplier's name and Business Number, the recipient's identity, the transaction description, and the GST/HST charged or a zero-rating indicator. GST/HST returns are filed periodically via GST/HST NETFILE; registrants with annual taxable supplies above CAD 1.5 million must file electronically. The CRA participates voluntarily in the Pan-Canadian Peppol-based e-invoice interoperability framework, but issuance is optional and is not a fiscal clearance requirement. Books and records must be retained for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating eligibility derives from Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. (1) Goods: a sale is zero-rated where the supplier exports the goods as soon as is reasonable after title passes or delivers them to a common carrier for export; CBSA export reporting and shipping records must evidence foreign delivery. (2) Services: a service supplied to a non-resident person is zero-rated unless the service is rendered to an individual present in Canada, is in respect of real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada, or is acquired for consumption, use, or enjoyment in Canada. (3) Intangible personal property: software, code libraries, digital templates, and online platform access supplied to a non-resident for use exclusively outside Canada are zero-rated. For a low-code/no-code website builder offering subscriptions through Stripe or Paddle to foreign B2B customers, export zero-rating applies if the recipient is non-resident and the digital service is not consumed in Canada; the supplier must retain evidence of the recipient's non-resident status (foreign incorporation, registered address, payment bank jurisdiction, IP geolocation, and service contract).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Export Declaration (Form B13A) filed electronically with the Canada Border Services Agency or an approved service provider, or the equivalent carrier export manifest
Bill of Lading (ocean/air/rail/truck) or courier airway bill evidencing export from Canada and delivery to the foreign consignee

Inward payment / foreign exchange remittance evidence: bank transfer, SWIFT/ISO 20022 message, or payment service provider settlement report. Canada does not operate an Inward Remittance Certificate regime; CRA accepts interbank payment records as export substantiation.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA audits export zero-rating claims by matching GST/HST returns with CBSA trade data; where documentary proof is absent, the supply is recharacterized as taxable and the 5% GST is assessed with compound daily interest. Civil penalties under section 285 of the Excise Tax Act: knowingly or with gross negligence making a false statement or omission in an invoice, return, refund, or claim attracts a penalty of the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the tax or rebate concerned. Offences under section 286 ETA for fraudulent or deceptive export claims are punishable on summary conviction by a fine of CAD 1,000 to CAD 25,000 and/or imprisonment up to 12 months, and on indictment by a fine up to CAD 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. Retrospective clawback: the CRA may reverse input tax credits allocated to zero-rated exports, recover refunds paid, and extend the normal 4-year reassessment period indefinitely where misrepresentation, fraud, or neglect is shown. Non-resident suppliers may be required to post security. Good-faith errors may be mitigated through a Voluntary Disclosure Program application or treaty mutual agreement procedure, but deliberate export fraud disqualifies relief. Although no express statutory FX-repatriation deadline applies in Canada, an 180-day benchmark is commonly used as payment-and-remittance substantiation in CRA export reviews; failure to demonstrate foreign-currency repatriation within that window may trigger denial of zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility. There are no exchange controls and no restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distributions, or capital repatriation for Canadian-resident or non-resident-owned corporations. Payments to non-residents do not require central bank approval, provided that applicable Part XIII withholding taxes are satisfied and cross-border transaction reports are filed through FINTRAC for transfers exceeding CAD 10,000 (or foreign-currency equivalent). The Canadian dollar floats freely; intervention by the Bank of Canada occurs only exceptionally. The Department of Finance governs foreign-exchange policy, while the Bank of Canada acts as fiscal agent for the Government of Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada does not impose mandatory surrender, conversion timelines, or repatriation quotas for export proceeds. Exporters may hold receipts in any freely convertible world currency, and there is no obligation to convert to CAD within any statutory period. Cross-border movements of currency or monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more require CBSA reporting; banking transactions may trigger FINTRAC large-transaction and cross-border wire reports. Export documentation (e.g., B13A Export Report) is required under the Customs Act for goods, but solely for customs statistics, not for foreign-exchange disposal.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account with Borderless US/Canada Banking
Operating Account + Foreign Currency Business Account
Operating Account + US Dollar Business Account
Operating Account for Technology Professionals + USD Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability as an ancillary settlement rail for Stripe Billing and Paddle payouts, particularly for USD/EUR receipt conversion and small-value global disbursements. However, offshore EMI balances are not CDIC-insured and cannot serve as the primary treasury depository. EMIs must comply with PCMLTFA customer identification and AML requirements, but major Canadian Schedule I banks generally require that final settlement of third-party merchant payouts occur into a CDIC-insured Canadian corporate bank account to minimise counterparty risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For standard-risk Alberta corporations, remote account opening is permitted using certified corporate documents, owner photo ID, video identity verification, and digital signing. If a director, beneficial owner, or signatory is non-resident or lacks a Canadian credit profile, most Schedule I banks apply a 'Medium' physical-presence mandate: an in-branch appointment for the instructing director (or a Canadian-licensed lawyer/agent holding a notarized power of attorney) is commonly required before account activation. The mandate becomes 'High' when PEP exposure or jurisdiction risk is present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or director appears as a politically exposed person (PEP) or is resident in a FATF grey-listed jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP risk assessment letter, source-of-funds declaration with three months of bank statements, notarized passport and proof of address, Alberta corporate registry extract with full shareholder register, independent legal opinion on beneficial ownership, and a notarized explanation of the lawful origin of invested funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of Canadian substantive nexus — no physical office, no Canadian employees, revenues generated entirely through Stripe Billing and Paddle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed terms of service, platform merchant agreements, subcontractor contracts, Canadian registered agent and mailing address, Alberta Business Registry certificate, detailed go-to-market plan with anticipated Canadian sales, and (if needed) a parent-company guarantee or affiliate agreement evidencing commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated e-commerce chargeback or refund volatility typical of low-code website builders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI DSS attestation, chargeback monitoring report, refund policy archive, man-in-the-proxy merchant-of-record agreement with Paddle, settlement-account flow diagram showing escrowed chargeback cover, and a financial projections model validating banks are not exposed to reputational risk.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from shareholders, venture investors, or parent entities must be wired via SWIFT MT103 using the beneficiary name exactly as registered in Alberta, the 9-digit Canadian transit and account number, and ISOCEDEX purpose code INV (Direct Investment) or G10 (Services). The remittance advice must reference the underlying transaction (e.g., 'shareholder loan', 'equity subscription', 'Stripe payout settlement'). For any single credit exceeding CAD 10,000 (or FX equivalent), the receiving institution files a FINTRAC large-currency transaction report; to prevent rejection, provide the corporate status certificate, proof of source of funds, and, when applicable, a completed Form T106 (Information Return for Non-Resident Arms-Length Equity Investments) or T1134 foreign affiliate schedule. Settlement to the CAD operating account clears via Lynx or ACSS; USD capital is parked in a dedicated USD account and converted only as treasury policy dictates.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for subcontractor fees, software licensing, marketing, and infrastructure procurement are cleared through SWIFT MT103 with structured ISO 20022 remittance tags (e.g., 'INV' for invoice, 'SUPP' for supplier). For high-value international contracts, an irrevocable confirmed commercial letter of credit (MT700) is recommended to eliminate counterparty risk. CAD payments are cleared via Lynx (high-value) or ACSS (ACH equivalent); USD payments may use Fedwire or CHIPS through a US correspondent account. All payments to non-residents must be accompanied by appropriate Part XIII withholding certifications (e.g., NR301 for GST/HST registrants, NR303 for non-arm's-length services) and, where applicable, Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Form T274 for treaty-basis withholding exemptions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright CAD/USD exchange-traded futures and negotiated OTC forward contracts
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currency receipts (e.g., Indian rupee, Philippine peso, Brazilian real)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for multi-currency term debt facilities
European-style FX options (puts and calls) to hedge committed payables and anticipated receivables
FX swaps for converting temporary cash surpluses without altering foreign-exchange net exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta, through the Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Registrar; intermediate enforcement includes registry default notices and potential late-filing administrative charges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return including Alberta corporate tax administered by the CRA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year end (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 year-end); instalment and balance-due payment deadlines apply under CRA rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month, up to 12 months; compound interest on unpaid balances; additional gross-negligence penalty where the omission is intentional.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold triggers a mandatory audit for a non-offering Alberta private corporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); an audit is required only if the corporation is an offering corporation or if shareholders fail to unanimously waive the appointment of an auditor. Lender, investor, or shareholder agreements may independently require audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises; a private no-code website builder corporation may adopt Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) under the CPA Canada Handbook. Tax accounting follows the Income Tax Act and CRA administrative rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not currently mandate a separate annual public beneficial-ownership filing for non-offering private corporations. Share transfers must be recorded in the corporate records at the time of transfer; the Alberta Annual Return requires confirmation of current directors, registered office, and general corporate status. Any federal or tax-driven UBO reporting (e.g., under the CBCA if the entity were federal) is outside the Alberta provincial secretarial process.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by default; if shareholder or lender demands an audit, a small Alberta private corporation typically incurs CAD 12,000–CAD 30,000 (approx. USD 9,000–USD 22,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday is available. Preferential rates and deductions include: the Federal Small Business Deduction reducing the federal rate to 9% and the Alberta rate to 2% on the first C$500,000 of active business income; SR&ED refundable investment tax credits; immediate expensing of eligible capital assets through capital cost allowance; and the non-capital loss carryforward of 20 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically with the Canada Revenue Agency through certified tax software via CRA EFILE or My Business Account. Alberta corporate income tax is assessed and collected by CRA under the Tax Collection Agreement; no separate Alberta corporate return is required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal-year); quarterly instalments of Part I corporate tax are normally required, with monthly instalments for large corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed within 6 months after the taxation year-end; the final balance of Canadian corporate tax is due within 2 months after year-end (3 months for a Canadian-controlled private corporation claiming the small-business deduction in that year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number (BN/RP), jurisdiction and federal incorporation status, fiscal year-end, address, director identification, and email contact for CRA correspondence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use a Canadian agent or representative address if applicable; indicate non-residency and Canadian permanent establishment (PE) information; include DTA residence facts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed income from software subscriptions, no-code website builder fees, hosting, royalties, and other business income; reconciled from financial statements to tax basis via Schedule 1.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income attributable to Canadian PE; claim treaty-protected income as non-taxable only if the DTA applies; enter on reconciliation schedules and attach DTA notes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply non-capital loss carryforwards, capital loss balances, inter-company dividends, and other Part I adjustments to derive taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the relevant treaty article governing income attribution; deduct losses that are carried forward under ITA s.111 and allocated to Alberta; non-resident loss history must be substantiated with prior T2 filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 24 - Provincial and Territorial Tax Allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocate taxable income between Alberta and other provinces based on permanent establishment formula (sales and salaries); compute Alberta corporate tax using the 8% Alberta general rate or 2% Alberta small business rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident and non-resident corporations with an Alberta PE must allocate income to Alberta; specify PE address and attributes; attach cross-border employee and service allocation details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all related-party cross-border transactions (software development, IP licensing, cloud services, cost sharing, royalties) together with transfer pricing method and functional analysis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File T106 even if transactions are treaty-exempt if the aggregate value exceeds the threshold; attach the contemporaneous transfer pricing study and document the arm's length standard.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty under ITA s.162(1): 5% of the unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay, to a maximum of 12 months. Repeated failures trigger the doubled 5% base under s.162(2). CRA imposes prescribed daily compound interest on balances (9% per annum in early 2025). Where no balance is due, late filing may attract a penalty up to C$500 and loss of CRA refund interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on taxable dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to a non-resident shareholder under Part XIII ITA; Alberta does not levy an additional provincial withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA withholding rate, the payer must obtain before payment: (1) Form NR301 (or NR302 where applicable) declaring treaty eligibility; (2) a Certificate of Tax Residence / TRC issued by the foreign tax authority; and (3) confirmation that the beneficial owner has no Canadian permanent establishment. Forms must be renewed annually and retained with tax records. If incomplete or absent, withhold at the statutory 25% rate; if a false declaration is used, the payer and payee remain jointly liable for the shortfall, interest, and penalties. Excess withheld tax can be recovered by filing a Canadian corporate tax return or a Form NR7 request for amended determination.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates under Part XIII: 25% for royalties and 25% for interest. Under the Canada-United States treaty, arm's length interest is generally exempt (0%), and software/patent/know-how royalties are generally capped at 10%; many Canadian DTAs reduce royalty withholding to 5-15% and interest withholding to 0-15% on arm's length debt. The applicable rate is conditional on beneficial ownership, absence of a PE, and submission of treaty relief documentation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No de minimis statutory threshold for transfer pricing documentation; CRA expects contemporaneous TP documentation for all non-arm's length cross-border transactions. Form T106 filing threshold is C$1,000,000 aggregate fair-market value of specified non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents. Country-by-Country Report and Master File / Local File obligations apply to multinational groups with consolidated group revenue equal to or exceeding C$880 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have offshore-tribunal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) akin to the UAE, but economic substance is central to corporate residence, permanent establishment, treaty eligibility, and Part I taxation. Under the GAAR (ITA s.245), arrangements lacking genuine commercial substance and used solely for tax-motivated purposes can be recharacterized. DTAs contain limitation-of-benefits-type rules and general anti-abuse principles that require real business activity, employees, premises, and risk management in Alberta and in any foreign intermediate entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of no-code platform subscription revenue, off-book Stripe/Paddle gross receipts, fabricated intercompany invoices, or false T2 filings designed to shift profits out of Alberta.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s.239(1): fine of 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment for up to 5 years; civil gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax under s.163(2); compound daily interest at the prescribed rate; CRA may freeze accounts and certificate liabilities as judgments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly committed evasion are criminally liable and subject to imprisonment; courts may impose restitution, asset freezes, travel restrictions or bans, and lift the corporate veil to hold directors jointly and severally liable for the evaded taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transacting with a related non-resident software holding company, IP owner, or subcontractor at non-arm's-length prices without contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation or Form T106 filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s.247(3) penalty of 10% of the net upward adjustment where documentation is insufficient; CRA may also reallocate income, deny tax deduction erosion, and apply interest. Failure to file T106 attracts additional penalties, and GAAR may be applied in egregious cross-border schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in approving false transfer pricing statements may be held grossly negligent, personally liable upon corporate insolvency, and vulnerable to criminal fraud charges if the transfer pricing structure is used as a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining employees in Alberta and collecting GST/HST on Stripe/Paddle subscription payments while withholding source deductions or GST/HST amounts without remitting them to CRA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s.227 and Excise Tax Act s.316 impose the full unremitted amount, a 10% additional penalty on amounts unpaid after 3 months, and prescribed daily compound interest. CRA may register liens on corporate assets and send third-party demand letters to processor accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable under ITA s.227.1 and Excise Tax Act s.323 for up to 100% of the unremitted source deductions and GST/HST without fault, if they knew or reasonably should have known of the failure; the corporate veil is pierced by statute.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Alberta corporation as a brass-plate conduit with no real directors' meetings, no employees, and no Alberta substance, while funneling Stripe/Paddle receipts through foreign accounts and omitting beneficial ownership registrations or suspicious transaction reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, failure to implement KYC/CDD and report suspicious transactions attracts significant administrative monetary penalties for corporations and criminal prosecution; Alberta's corporate registry may dissolve a non-compliant corporation; CRA may treat the structure as an avoidance arrangement under GAAR and impose all applicable taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominees and directors of a sham corporation may be charged with aiding unlawful activity, face civil restitution, asset confiscation proceedings, travel bans, and imprisonment for up to 5 years where the enterprise is used for money laundering or tax evasion.
